deterministic.summary: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting (protective response, not the origin). Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. The recorded data does not separate them. A weak cell cannot explain the whole incident on its own: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation. No root cause is confirmed.

result.headline: BMS under-voltage trip at 2100.5 s after SOC overstated by about 56 points; cause of the overstatement is open
result.explanation: HV opened as the BMS's under-voltage protection. SOC fell only about 4.4 points while the cells fell to the cutoff, then dropped to 1.2 %. SOC error, low usable capacity or current under-reading all fit the recording.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 7.81 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: Constant 7.81 A (about 4.6 Ah measured over the run) was far too little charge to account for 60 % of 100 Ah.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=2394.5 s: 56 -> 1.2 % (step -54.8, 45.7x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: An abrupt correction of the SOC by about 55 points: the estimate had been counting charge only.
Level 3 fault coincides with both contactors opening (lines 19-20), after levels 1 and 2 at 1453 s and 1799 s.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=628 s: median 3.2 before, 2.841 after V (3590x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The cell voltage shifted down at 628 s, about 1470 s before the trip, while SOC stayed near 57-58 %.
HV was reclosed three times at SOC 1.2 % and tripped again each time.

checked.check: Charge accounting: does SOC follow measured current?
checked.result: SOC tracked measured charge / about 100 Ah (ratios 0.922 and 1.024). This is by construction, so it shows counting and not that capacity or current is right.
checked.about: SOC estimation / calibration error, usable capacity and current measurement

checked.check: Energy shortfall: measured Ah delivered against the Ah the SOC promised
checked.result: About 4.6 Ah delivered against 60.4 Ah promised. That needs SOC overstated by about 56 points, or capacity of about 8 Ah, or current under-read by about 13x. A and B and C each need a very large error alone.
checked.about: SOC estimation / calibration error, usable capacity and current measurement

checked.result: Fault levels went 1 -> 2 -> 3 over 1453-2100.5 s, and the contactors opened at 2100.5 s with level 3. The order runs from cell under-voltage to contactor opening.
checked.about: Contactor, VCU or insulation event first

checked.check: Weak-cell test: is the lowest cell alone low?
checked.result: Cell 66 was lowest in 100 % of samples, but the highest cell fell 450 mV, more than the 260 mV spread at the trip. The pack as a whole was depleted.

checked.check: Sensing fault test: smoothness and rest recovery
checked.result: Lowest-cell samples never jumped by more than 1 mV. Cells recovered to 2.28-2.59 V with HV open. This fits a real cell and not a sense-lead fault.
No lessons and no verified earlier knowledge apply.

effects.why: Protective response to the level 3 under-voltage escalation. It is how HV was lost, not why the cells were low.

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.pack_current at t=2094.5 s: 7.81 -> 0 A (step -7.81, 1000x its usual variation)
effects.why: Current went to zero at the HV opening; the recording does not show who commanded it.

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=2394.5 s: 56 -> 1.2 % (step -54.8, 45.7x its usual variation)
effects.why: A late correction of the SOC estimate, not a physical discharge.
Repeat trips after HV reclosure at low SOC are consequences of the depleted pack.

safety_findings.statement: Do not close HV or charge until every cell's rest voltage is assessed. The lowest cell reached 2.421 V on reclosure, below the 2.500 V original trip level.
HV was reclosed three times after protective shutdowns into deeper discharge than the original trip. Review the restart policy.
HV was closed 3 times after the protective shutdown at 2100.5 s: at 3266.5, 3320.8 and 3404.5 s. Whether this was permitted depends on a restart policy not available here.
Each of the 3 closures ended in another protective shutdown (3285.0, 3339.3, 3422.5 s). Repeated closing into a depleted pack is a risk; review before any further closure.
The 3 closures followed a fault reset that the record does not show (it fell in a gap or before the window). Who or what reset the fault is unknown.

unknowns: Why SOC was overstated by about 56 points: estimator drift, low capacity or current under-reading cannot be separated from this data.
Chemistry, series count, protection thresholds and restart policy are not stated, so the protection sequence cannot be judged.
What caused the cell voltage level shifts at 628 s and 685 s; the data shows them but does not explain them.

physical.summary: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting (protective response, not the origin). Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. The recorded data does not separate them. A weak cell cannot explain the whole incident on its own: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation. No root cause is confirmed.

constrained_claims.text: BMS under-voltage trip at 2100.5 s after SOC overstated by about 56 points; cause of the overstatement is open

HV opened as the BMS's under-voltage protection. SOC fell only about 4.4 points while the cells fell to the cutoff, then dropped to 1.2 %. SOC error, low usable capacity or current under-reading all fit the recording.
SOC estimation / calibration: SOC drifted high by coulomb counting without effective correction and was corrected only at the under-voltage alarm.
reasons: consistent with SOC estimation / calibration error (open)

constrained_claims.text: Usable capacity below parameter: Usable capacity is far below the 100 Ah the SOC is computed against.
reasons: consistent with Usable capacity far below the stated parameter (open)

constrained_claims.text: Current measurement path: The current sensor under-reads, or a load bypasses it, so counted charge is below real discharge.
reasons: consistent with Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor (open)

constrained_claims.text: Weak cell / imbalance: Cell 66 is weaker or poorly balanced and reaches cutoff first.
Cell-voltage sensing / harness: The low cell reading is a sense-lead or channel error.
reasons: consistent with Cell-voltage sensing or harness fault (weakened)

constrained_claims.text: Contactor / VCU / insulation first: A contactor, VCU or insulation fault came first and the battery alarms followed.
reasons: consistent with Contactor, VCU or insulation event first (weakened)
